sources.entry: Baïkal - Lightweight CalDAV and CardDAV server based on sabre/dav. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: Baïkal is a lightweight CalDAV and CardDAV server built on sabre/dav for syncing calendars and contacts.
summary.what_it_does: The README is short and points to sabre.io/baikal for installation, upgrade and troubleshooting details. It describes Baïkal as the source repository for a CalDAV and CardDAV server. It links to community tutorials: a German guide covering installation, use with Thunderbird, Android and DavX5, calendar sharing, database maintenance and security, and a French guide covering Debian installation, database maintenance, security and iOS clients. The README also documents how to run the test suite, either against SQLite with the PHP built-in server or against all databases via Docker Compose. Credits name Jérôme Schneider and fruux as creators, with the project now maintained by volunteers. The listing describes it as lightweight and based on sabre/dav.
use_cases: CalDAV server for Thunderbird or Android
share calendars with family or team
notable: Implements both CalDAV (calendars) and CardDAV (contacts) in one lightweight server
Official install and upgrade documentation lives at sabre.io/baikal rather than in the repo
Test suite can run against SQLite or multiple databases via Docker
caveats: The test suite resets configuration and database, so it must not be run on a real installation
Installation and upgrade details are not in this README; they are on an external site
Maintained by volunteers, per the README
